originality.rationale: The primary paper arXiv:2109.11101v2, Section IV equation (29), Fig. 9, reports fitted effective exponents .352 and -.625 and numerical prefactors .532 and 29.59, rather than the mathematically exact small-inner-radius exponents 1/3 and -2/3, limiting constants, and correction coefficient. Exhaustive comparison of the relevant analytic and discussion portions confirms that it gives no equivalent globally justified asymptotic. The one-dimensional interval treatment arXiv:1812.03009 does not imply the three-dimensional small-hole saddle; actual semantic searches yielded no exact match, not a proof of universal absence.

value.rationale: The motivating primary study explicitly investigates an inner first-order transition and reports fitted effective exponents. Establishing the true critical singular balance between capture by a tiny inner sphere and conventional outer-sphere exit, with exact leading and correction coefficients and a proof of global-optimality selection, answers a concrete outstanding asymptotic question and provides reliable scaling for extrapolation beyond finite c. It is not a mere numerical improvement or textbook substitution.
